transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My insurance physical, the doctor there said my weight was too low and thought I should get it checked. I don’t really see it that way... I mean, I’m on ladders all day, long hours painting, so I’ve always figured I’m just lean.
Do you think you are underweight?
Not really. I mean, I know my friends and the doctor are worried, but… I’m still getting to work, doing my jobs. So it feels like maybe they’re making more of it than it is.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I don’t know if I’d call it afraid exactly… but if the scale goes up even a little, like after a client dinner or eating bread, I get pretty tense. Usually I’ll cut back the next day so it doesn’t… stay there.
Do you often limit the types or amounts of food you eat?
Yeah… I guess I do. Most days it’s just coffee, maybe a protein bar between jobs, and then a small dinner. A full meal feels like it’d slow me down, so I usually don’t bother.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yeah… I guess so. Not like panic, but if the scale’s up even a little after a dinner or bread or something, I get really tense. Then I usually cut back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
Do you think your weight is a problem because of how you think you look?
Yeah… kind of. If I see myself in a mirror, or in photos by one of my murals, I end up checking whether my stomach or my face looks… sharp enough. It can sort of set the tone for the whole day.
When you think about gaining weight, what is it about your body that you're most concerned would change?
Mostly my stomach… and my face, I guess. If they don’t look sharp enough in a mirror or a photo, it kind of gets in my head for the rest of the day.
Do you think there's a specific weight that you should be at to look the way you want?
Not really a number exactly… it’s more what I see. Like if I catch myself in a mirror, or in a photo next to one of my murals, I sort of judge it by whether my stomach and face look sharp enough.
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if you could maintain the sharpness in your face and stomach?

I think so, yeah. Even if that stayed the same… if the scale goes up a little, like after a client dinner or bread or something, I get tense. I usually try to cut back the next day so it doesn’t… stick.
Is your fear of gaining weight more about how your body would look or about the actual number on the scale?
It’s… both, I guess. How I look matters, but even if it’s just the number going up a little after a client dinner or bread, I get tense. Then I’ll usually cut back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
Do you feel like you would lose control if you started gaining weight?
Yeah… kind of. If the scale goes up even a little, like after a dinner or something with bread, I get tense. I feel like I have to cut back the next day so it doesn’t… stay there.
Do you feel like you're in control of your weight right now?
Mostly, I guess. I keep a pretty close eye on it. If it goes up even a little, like after a dinner or bread, I get tense and cut back the next day so it doesn’t… stay.
Do you think gaining weight would mean you've failed in some way to control your body?
Yeah… I guess it feels that way. Like if the scale goes up even a little after a client dinner or bread, I get tense. Then I feel like I have to cut back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
Do you feel like gaining weight would mean you're no longer in control of your body?
Yeah… I think so. If it goes up even a little, especially after a client dinner or bread, I get really tense. I end up cutting back the next day so it doesn’t… stay.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about feeling like you'd lose control over your body?
Yeah… mostly. When the scale is up even a little, like after a client dinner or bread, I get tense. Then I try to cut back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
Is your fear of gaining weight more about how you think your body would look or about feeling like you're losing control?

More control, I think. I mean… I don’t like how I’d look either, but what really gets me is the scale going up. If it’s even a little after dinner out or bread, I get tense and cut back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because you believe you would look unattractive if you gained weight?

Some of it, yeah. I don’t like saying that, but… if I see myself in a mirror or a photo, especially by one of my murals, I’ll kind of judge the whole day by whether my face and stomach look… sharp enough.
Is your goal to maintain a specific body shape or to avoid being a certain weight?
More the shape, I guess. Like… if I catch myself in a mirror, or in a photo next to one of my murals, I’ll sort of decide how the day’s going by whether my stomach and face look sharp enough.
Is your fear of gaining weight more about losing control of your eating or about how your body would look?
More the losing control part, I think. Like if the scale is up even a little after a client dinner or something with bread, I get… tense. Then I start cutting back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
Is your fear of gaining weight because you think you would eat too much if you weren't constantly watching what you eat?

Yeah… I think so. If I’m not watching it, it feels like it could get away from me. Like if the scale is up even a little after a dinner or bread or whatever, I get tense and cut back the next day so it doesn’t… stick.
